# Lexicon

> Speech-to-text gets English right and your names wrong. Lexicon is one YAML file of the words a person actually says. It rewrites the transcript before an agent reads it. It is not a dictation app.

Agents are first-class users. Do not install it unasked. Preview, show the plan, then apply.

Install (Node 20+). The script runs `lexicon setup` when it has a terminal. Without a terminal, under `sudo`, or with `LEXICON_NO_SETUP=1`, it only installs and ends with `run: lexicon setup`.

```bash
curl -fsSL https://ashlrai.github.io/lexicon/install.sh | sh
```

No global install:

```bash
npx @ashlr/lexicon@latest setup
```

Preview, write nothing:

```bash
lexicon setup --dry-run --json
```

Correct a transcript. Stdout is one JSON document. Read `ok`, then `output`. `example: true` means the built-in sample stood in and nothing was written.

```bash
lexicon normalize "ask ashler to deploy kuber netties with post gressql" --json
```

One stable shape for every command: append `--json=v1` instead. Stdout is `{ schemaVersion: 1, ok, data }`, where `data` is the command's usual `--json` result; a refusal carries `data.error` and `data.nextStep`. `mcp`, `hook`, `edit`, `review` and the continuous clipboard watcher refuse it. Details: [docs/CLI-JSON.md](docs/CLI-JSON.md).

```bash
lexicon normalize "ask ashler to deploy kuber netties with post gressql" --json=v1
```

MCP server. Preview (`applied` is false), then write:

```bash
lexicon install claude --json
lexicon install claude --apply --json
lexicon install cursor --json
lexicon install cursor --apply --json
lexicon install codex --json
lexicon install codex --apply --json
```

Hand config, only when `lexicon-mcp` is on PATH.

Claude Code and Cursor (`~/.cursor/mcp.json`):

    {
      "mcpServers": {
        "lexicon": { "command": "lexicon-mcp", "args": [] }
      }
    }

Codex (`~/.codex/config.toml`):

    [mcp_servers.lexicon]
    command = "lexicon-mcp"
    args = []

## Part of the Ashlr.AI ecosystem

Phantom and its ecosystem form a fully autonomous, code-first, agent-native software factory, run by agents with the human as a passive board member, chasing open source RSI (recursive self improvement). Lexicon is the voice layer: it makes sure the names a person dictates reach those agents spelled right.

- Phantom: the agent-run software factory the rest of the ecosystem serves.
- phantom-secrets: `phantom exec` gives an agent `phm_` placeholders instead of real provider keys. Lexicon needs no key and runs unchanged under it.
- ashlr-plugin: the Claude Code plugin for agent tooling.
- Locus: identity and tenant pinning for agents.
- lexicon: this project.
- ashlr-md: ships `mdopener-mcp`.
- ashlr-stack: the `stack` CLI; it owns the shared handshake contract.

Lexicon runs without any of the others. `lexicon doctor` asks `locus` and `mdopener-mcp` for `--ashlr-handshake --json` and reports one info line for each; a missing companion is not an error.

Agents write and ship this code. To change it, read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), then [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md). Contributors and their agents follow the same path: [Contribute with an agent](CONTRIBUTING.md#contribute-with-an-agent) (fork, `npm ci`, `lexicon test-select`, the commands the required `CI Gate` check runs, the merge queue). The merge queue reruns `CI Gate` on the branch merged with current `main` and squash-merges it when green; no approving review is required and the branch need not be up to date. Auto-merge (`gh pr merge --auto`) needs write access, so on a fork pull request a maintainer or the fleet arms it.
